title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics for an 'analysis situs' (a tame, combinatorial topology in the spirit of the 'topologie modérée' of Esquisse d'un programme). A structure ('contrée'?) is a triple (𝓕, ≤, ≼). 𝓕 is a set of 'figures' (think finite polyhedral or simplicial complexes inside a fixed ambient space). G ≤ F means G is a sub-figure (subcomplex) of F. F' ≼ F means F' is a subdivision of F. He is listing axioms C1, C2, … that relate the two orders.

Top of page (end of the definition from p.71). By axiom C6, for F' ≼ F and G ≤ F there is a unique G' with G' ≤ F' and G' ≼ G. This G' is called the trace: 'the sub-figure of the subdivision F' of F induced by the sub-figure G of F'. Geometrically, G' is the restriction of the subdivision F' to |G|. In lattice terms it is a pullback of the subobject G along the subdivision F' → F.

Axiom C7₀. For every figure F, sub-figure G ≤ F and subdivision G' ≼ G, there exists a subdivision F' ≼ F whose trace on G is G'. In modern terms: every subdivision of a subcomplex extends to a subdivision of the whole complex. This is a standard PL lemma, proved by inductive coning or derived subdivision away from the subcomplex.

He notes that the 'symmetric' statement (swapping the roles of ≤ and ≼) is false. Given F' ≼ F, not every sub-figure of F' is induced by a sub-figure of F. For example, a small simplex created by subdividing a triangle is not the trace of any subcomplex of the triangle. So the axiom system is deliberately asymmetric in the two orders. This answers the marginal question 'symétrique pour ≤, ≼ ?' raised on p.71.

He announces a strengthening C7 that makes a canonical choice of the extension F'.

Crossed-out passage. For two figures F, G he compares:
(a) G ≤ F' ≼ F (G is a sub-figure of a subdivision of F);
(b) G ≼ G' ≤ F (G is a subdivision of a sub-figure of F).
He first called them 'equivalent', then struck that word. He records b) ⇒ a) via C7₀: extend the subdivision G of G' to a subdivision F' of F, so that G ≤ F'. He records that a) ⇒ b) fails ('!!!') and crosses out the claim that it follows from C6.

The diagram F ≽ F' over G … G' summarizes the square. The outcome feeds the next page. There condition (a) becomes the definition of 'raffinement' G ≪ F. He then proves ≪ is a partial order (transitivity via C6, C7; antisymmetry via a lemma), combining the two orders into one.
errors: No mathematical error in the final text.
The crossed-out passage contained a false equivalence: a) ⇒ b) fails. Grothendieck caught this himself and struck it, which is why the next page defines refinement by a) alone.

For the strengthened C7 ('choix canonique'), true canonicity is delicate in PL. Coning or derived extensions depend on choices of interior points, so 'canonical' must presumably be read inside a fixed tame / semi-linear framework. This is not addressed here.

ideas.what: Trace (restriction) of a subdivision F' of F to a sub-figure G, as the unique G' ≤ F' with G' ≼ G
ideas.modern_name: induced subdivision on a subcomplex; pullback of a subobject along a refinement

ideas.what: Axiom C7₀: every subdivision of a subcomplex extends to a subdivision of the whole complex
ideas.modern_name: extension of subdivisions (standard PL lemma; analogue of cell decompositions adapted to subsets in o-minimal geometry)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology (e.g. Rourke–Sanderson, Hudson); o-minimal analogue van den Dries

ideas.what: Observation that the axiom is asymmetric in ≤ and ≼: sub-figures of a subdivision need not be traces of sub-figures
ideas.modern_name: failure of a lifting property / non-symmetric interaction of the two orders

ideas.what: Comparison of 'sub-figure of a subdivision' versus 'subdivision of a sub-figure', leading to the refinement order G ≪ F defined by G ≤ F' ≼ F
ideas.modern_name: composite order generated by inclusion and refinement (factorization of PL embeddings of triangulated subpolyhedra)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches tame topology programmatically, without this axiomatics

missed.claim: Grothendieck's abstract axiomatics of 'contrées' (𝓕, ≤, ≼), with axioms such as C6/C7 linking sub-figures and subdivisions, is an attempted order-theoretic foundation for tame topology. To my knowledge it was never developed in the literature. This page fixes one axiom (extension of subdivisions) and an asymmetry that the later refinement order depends on.
missed.quote: Pour toute figure F, sous-figure G, et subdivision G' de G, il existe une subdivision F' de F qui induise G'.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a synthetic, two-order axiomatics that could be compared with o-minimal cell-decomposition axioms or with abstract 'subdivision categories'. Its interest is in the overall framework rather than in this page's lemma, which is standard PL.

deep.surprise_reason: The content of this page is a standard PL fact (subdivisions extend from subcomplexes), recast as an axiom, plus a correct observation that the axioms are asymmetric. Its only interest is as one piece of the unpublished axiomatic tame-topology program.
transcription_corrections: 'pour F' ⋖ F divisée' should read approximately 'pour F' ≼ F donnés'. The relation symbol throughout is ≼ (subdivision), not ⋖.
'On [-peut-] renforcerait [?] par C [-dite-] C7_o en C7' is better read as 'On renforcera par la suite C7₀ en C7, en prenant un choix canonique de F''.
In the crossed-out block, the word struck after 'Conditions' is 'équivalentes'. The deletion is meaningful, since the conditions are not equivalent.
'(Mais pas inv. a ⇒ b !!!)' should read '(Mais pas vrai a ⇒ b !!!)'. The image reads roughly 'Mais pas vrai a⇒b', within a crossed region.
The diagram reads F ≽ F' on top, G ≤ F vertically (∪), a dotted vertical from F' to G', and G … G' on the bottom row.
